meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I knew someone had to take the first step and I made up my mind not to move'?
meta.ogDescription: The sentiment is Parks’s own and well documented. This particular sentence has no named source.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Parks spent the rest of her life correcting the idea that she stayed seated because her feet hurt, so a line about having decided in advance is exactly the point she kept making. But this particular sentence has no source: Wikiquote lists it on the talk page under “Unsourced,” and it does not appear in the full text of her papers at the Library of Congress. What is documented is a sharper sentence from her autobiography — “the only tired I was, was tired of giving in.”
answer.confidenceText: The thought is demonstrably hers. This wording is not pinned to any publication.

source.excerpt: I knew someone had to take the first step and I made up my mind not to move.
trail: Wikiquote puts this one on the talk page, not the article. It is listed under “Unsourced” on Talk:Rosa Parks ↗, among lines editors could not attach to a publication.

The documented version of the thought is better. Wikiquote’s sourced list ↗ carries “People always said that I didn’t give up my seat because I was tired, but that isn’t true… the only tired I was, was tired of giving in,” which it cites to Rosa Parks: My Story, p. 116 (Parks and James Haskins, 1992). We are reporting Wikiquote’s citation here; the book itself was not readable from this session.

Her papers do not contain the phrase. A full-text search of the Rosa Parks Papers ↗ for “made up my mind not to move” returns nothing — a signal, though the digitised collection is partial and handwriting OCR is imperfect.
No specialist has traced it. Quote Investigator, which this site defers to wherever it has investigated a line, has no article on this one, so there is no earlier attestation on record to adopt.

author.name: Rosa Parks
author.kicker: The woman who would not move
author.heading: About Rosa Parks
author.metaLine: 1913–2005 · American civil rights activist · Montgomery, Alabama
author.bio: Rosa Louise McCauley Parks was a seamstress and long-serving NAACP secretary in Montgomery, Alabama, whose refusal to give up her bus seat on 1 December 1955 set off the Montgomery bus boycott. Congress later called her the Mother of the Modern-Day Civil Rights Movement, a title that has had the odd side effect of attracting inspirational sentences she never demonstrably wrote. She published an autobiography, Rosa Parks: My Story, with James Haskins in 1992, and her papers are held at the Library of Congress.

context.heading: Why the wording matters here
lead: Parks was not a tired seamstress who happened to snap. She was a trained organiser and the secretary of the Montgomery NAACP, and she objected for the rest of her life to the version of the story in which she simply had sore feet. A quotation about having made up her mind in advance therefore lands on exactly the right side of the argument.

Which is precisely why it is worth checking rather than repeating. The correction is well documented in her own book; this sentence is a paraphrase of it that has drifted loose from any source, and you do not need the loose one when the documented one is sharper.
context.pull: The point is real and sourced. This particular sentence is neither.

sourcesVerified.claim: The talk page of the English Wikiquote article "Rosa Parks" lists, under the heading "Unsourced", the sentence "I knew someone had to take the first step and I made up my mind not to move."

A full-text search of the Library of Congress Rosa Parks Papers collection for the exact phrase "made up my mind not to move" returns zero results, against a validated search (control phrase "tired of giving in" returns one result).

The English Wikiquote article "Rosa Parks" lists roughly a dozen quotations that each carry a named source (Rosa Parks: My Story p. 116; an NPR interview of 1992; a 1995 Washington speech; Theoharis's The Rebellious Life of Mrs. Rosa Parks).
The talk page of the English Wikiquote article "Rosa Parks" carries a section headed "Unsourced" listing quotations attributed to Parks that editors could not tie to a publication.

Wikiquote's sourced section gives "People always said that I didn't give up my seat because I was tired, but that isn't true... the only tired I was, was tired of giving in," citing Rosa Parks: My Story, p. 116, Rosa Parks and James Haskins (1992).

The Internet Archive holds a scan of "Rosa Parks: My Story" catalogued to Parks (1913-2005) and published by Puffin Books, dated 1999 in the item metadata; the full text is lending-restricted and could not be read or searched.

Wikipedia records Rosa Louise McCauley Parks as an American civil rights activist, 1913-2005, best known for her 1955 refusal to move from her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, which sparked the Montgomery bus boycott.
